title: The old dipper Gaia20cdd dims in two modes in ZTF 2018-2025: a smooth, thin small-grain medium with a steep extinction law covers it on most nights, and opaque clumps make the near-grey dips
abstract: Prior campaign studies of Gaia20cdd, a kinematically old K-type dipper star, used a fixed quiet level and did not agree on what makes its deep dips nearly grey. We separated the ZTF DR24 light curve (2018-2025, 738 nights with g and r) by colour, with 30 same-field comparison stars for zero points (seasonal g-r stable to 0.009 mag). Outside the deep dips the star fades and recovers by up to 0.3 mag in g over months to years. These slow changes follow k_g = A_g/A_r = 1.79 +- 0.04 and k_i = 0.66 +- 0.03 (585 nights), steeper than interstellar dust (1.42, 0.73). Nights deeper than 0.3 mag in the 2019-2022 dips follow k_g = 1.04 +- 0.04 and k_i = 0.95 +- 0.03. Seven analysis variants change these values by at most 0.09. A split of each night into a steep-law depth S and a near-grey depth D leaves D at the noise level outside the dips; S exceeds 0.05 mag on 75 percent of nights, is smooth on lags below 6 days (TESS 2024: 12-h rms 0.45 percent at a fade onset) and varies over 100-800 days. Mie models give slow-mode grains with a_max 0.05-0.23 um (astrosilicate), 0.03-0.10 um (graphite) or 0.37-0.47 um (ice). Optically thin large grains predict W1 depths of 1.1-5.8 mag in the 2022 dip, against 0.41 mag observed. Opaque clumps (r optical depth at least 6-12, cover 0.94) of the slow-mode grains plus the diffuse medium fit the g, r, i, W1 and W2 depths (chi2 2.6-9.2, 3 dof); pure-ice clumps fail. S rose from 0.03 to about 0.2 mag during the 2022 dip. The 2021 and 2024 maxima agree within 0.005 mag; a persistent screen of 0.96 mag, proposed to save the 2025 ice band, must be nearly grey. Thus one small-grain population forms dense clumps and a long-lived diffuse medium. Limitations: detections-only ZTF data, two fixed laws, spherical pure grains, one NEOWISE epoch, season-to-season law changes, no spectra. display.caption: Gaia20cdd in ZTF DR24, 2018-2025: g and r magnitudes, g-r colour, and the split of each night into a steep-law depth S (blue, slow) and a near-grey depth D (orange, deep dips). TESS 2024 sectors (grey) and the 2025 SPHEREx band visits (green) are marked.

Colour trajectories: slow-mode nights follow A_g = 1.79 A_r and A_i = 0.66 A_r; deep-dip nights follow a near-grey law (1.04 and 0.95) with a 0.15 mag g offset. The dashed line is diffuse interstellar dust.

It fitted the 2022 colour trajectory with one law and a uniform screen. We find two laws and show that opaque clumps, not large grains or a uniform screen, make the deep dips grey. We reuse its Mie code.
Its cloud-model degeneracy for the near-grey track agrees with our opaque-clump result.
It showed that ordinary icy dust needs at least 0.96 mag of persistent obscuration to explain the 2025 band; our stable maxima and slow-mode law show that such a screen must be nearly grey.
Reported the 2025 3.1 um band in the slow chromatic low state; our results place any ice in the diffuse medium.
